**Forecast consensus from the National Weather Service and local outlets centers on a high near 85°F for Denver on September 1, 2026, aligning with the market’s leading 84–85°F bin (57% implied probability) and the 86–87°F bin (33%).** 

At Denver’s elevation of roughly 5,280 feet, daytime heating under partly cloudy skies supports temperatures in the mid-80s, consistent with the long-term average high of 84.3°F for the date. Southwesterly flow, dew points in the low-to-mid 50s, and only modest afternoon thunderstorm chances (10–30% after 3 p.m.) limit excessive warming while still permitting peak readings around 84–86°F. Recent model runs and hourly guidance show afternoon temperatures plateauing near 85°F before any convective cooling, keeping the distribution tightly clustered in the low-to-mid 80s. 

Historical variability on September 1 (extremes from the 50s to the upper 90s) is acknowledged, yet current atmospheric conditions lack the strong high-pressure ridge or downslope warming needed for outliers above 88°F or below 82°F. Updated NWS and local forecasts issued early on September 1 reinforce this narrow range, explaining why traders have concentrated probability in the two leading outcomes.

Subtle differences among runs arise from the precise timing of daytime heating, boundary-layer mixing, and minor cloud-cover variations that can shift the peak by 1–2 °C. Historical climatology shows an average high of roughly 23 °C, so current guidance reflects a modest positive anomaly driven by a transient ridge. Updated model runs and Météo-France guidance issued in the next 24–48 hours will narrow the exact peak and determine whether traders continue to favor the 26–27 °C outcomes.

title: Highest temperature in Seoul (Incheon) on September 3?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Incheon Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rksi

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Warmer or cooler outliers carry low probability under the present synoptic pattern. Updated model runs and observational data over the next 24–48 hours will provide the clearest signals for any final adjustments.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Istanbul Airport in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=LTFM

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Cape Town International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=fact

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast model runs from agencies monitoring the region show a cool, windy September 3 in Cape Town driven by strong southeasterly flow and widespread cloud cover with showers, limiting daytime heating and keeping maximum temperatures in the 15–17 °C range. These conditions align with early-spring climatology, when Atlantic cold fronts and orographic effects often suppress highs below seasonal averages near 18 °C. Trader sentiment clusters on 15–17 °C outcomes because ensemble guidance converges on a midday peak near 15–16 °C under persistent onshore winds, though small timing shifts in rain or wind strength could nudge the exact maximum by 1 °C either way ahead of final observations.
